label: late-episode decay deepened by a2 / S2 history, lifted by reward
explanation: Raw candidate n of unit 33 sits near +1 early in the episode and falls steeply over the last ~30 trials (timing alone R^2 0.83). Beyond timing, the history effects are mostly multiplicative with that late decay (they are weighted by (ep_trial/99)^6): late in the episode the unit drops further after a2 choices (previous a2; this trial a2 at D2, where the choice is already observed) and at D1 after reaching S2, and it is lifted at D1 after a rewarded trial. At GO it is higher when the previous outcome points model-based toward a1 (S1 rewarded or S2 unrewarded) and higher with the a1-favouring policy logit. There are also small unscaled effects: GO up after S1 unrewarded and down after S2 rewarded, and D1 down after an unrewarded a2 trial. The many late-episode windows of repeated a2 choices are the deepest negative values. Every term is observable at its step (action is used only at D2; choice is the model policy logit). Dev R^2 beyond timing 0.48, test 0.45, above the additive all ceiling of 0.31 because of the lateness interaction. Without the lateness scaling, unscaled previous-trial indicators reach only about 0.10.

issues: The claim that it 'drops at D1 after the agent reached S2' is misattributed. Scored alone at D1, late-scaled prev_reward==1 (+0.56), prev_action==2 (-0.60) and prev_state==2 (-0.06) give test R^2 0.275, so the D1 drop comes from having CHOSEN a2, not from reaching S2. The residual table agrees: D1 after a2 S1 u is -0.137 and after a1 S2 r is +0.069. Swapping the D1 prev_state==2 term for a D1 prev_action==2 term raises test R^2 from 0.453 to 0.469. In that fit the D1 a2 weight is -0.47 and the generic late prev_action==2 term falls to about 0.

The late GO term 'higher when the outcome points a model-based agent toward a1' is weak. Alone it scores test R^2 0.005 beyond timing, and its weight falls to 0.009 once the D1 term is fixed. What is actually there late at GO is two separate effects: up after S1 (+0.42) and DOWN after a reward (-0.31), together 0.093. So 'lifted by reward' holds at D1 only. At GO, reward lowers the unit.

The non-scaled GO term (+ after S1 u, - after S2 r) scores 0.085 alone. That roughly matches the residual table, but GO after a1 S1 r (+0.064) and a2 S1 u (+0.073) are also up, so 'S1 raises it at GO' describes it more simply than an MB-direction framing.

A systematic error class remains. The worst-fit late windows (t85-t97) are off by a persistent offset of about +/-0.4 to 0.6 that holds across every step of the window. In one, the unit stays near +0.4 to 0.7 at GO and D2 over a2/S2 trials when -0.1 to -0.5 is predicted. In another, GO stays near -0.3 over repeated rewarded a1 S1 trials when +0.36 is predicted. (ep_trial/99)^6 is standing in for an episode-specific decay level that the terms do not capture. A smooth lateness term with no history scores only 0.05, so the history interaction is real, but the episode-level offset is unexplained.
The test R^2 of 0.453 is just at the 'explained' threshold, and several individual claims in the explanation are wrong or weak (see above), so the evidence is mixed.
skeptic.revised_label: late-episode decay deepened after choosing a2 (not reaching S2), lifted at D1 by reward; at GO raised after S1
